text:
alice: Heads up — we need a compact plan for request-ID propagation + sampling telemetry to power the rollout UX and a couple new dashboards. Looking for runtime + infra inputs: what headers will be emitted, who makes the sampling decision, and which metrics we can rely on. cc @brian @sasha @taylor

brian: Runtime status: we currently propagate `x-request-id` and `traceparent`. We can emit two counters per request: `rw.request.count{route,model,region}` and `rw.trace.sampled.count{route,model,region}`. Emitting a bool tag on spans (`request.id`) is easy.

sasha: +1 for deterministic sampling. If sampling is deterministic based on request-id hash the same logical request stays sampled across services even when routing changes. Pseudocode: `sampled = (hash(req_id) % 100) < sampling_pct`. That avoids losing traces when we route to dedicated vs hosted.

taylor: Console needs these concrete signals: `request.total`, `request.with_request_id`, `trace.sampled.count`, and `trace.ingest.bytes` (approx). We want to expose per-route sampling rate and a small control to override sample rate per-route in rollout mode. UX-wise: dropdown with baseline % + canary override.

maria: One catch — some frontends don't set request-id. We should define a guaranteed header `x-rw-request-id` and add a lightweight edge-fallback that generates a UUID if absent. Edge team can own generation.

brian: Agreed. Edge will generate `x-rw-request-id` if missing and set `x-rw-request-source: edge`. Runtime will not regenerate if present.

sasha: For metrics, prefer counters over histograms for sampled vs unsampled counts, so panels can compute sampled_ratio = `trace.sampled.count / request.total`. Also emit `request.id.present` (bool counter) to compute coverage.

taylor: Grafana panels we want: 1) sampled ratio by route/model/region, 2) request-id coverage by client type, 3) traces ingested per minute (billing protection), 4) list of top routes with high variance between sampled_ratio and expected sampling_pct.

alice: On the sampling decision ownership: do we want routing layer to decide, runtime to decide, or deterministic only? Pros/cons: routing can steer capacity-aware sampling; deterministic ensures stable correlation.

sasha: Suggest hybrid: deterministic hashing establishes a base sample. Routing layer can apply an upstream cap/floor by adding header `x-rw-sampled-override: force|deny|none`. Runtime respects override if present. That keeps correlation but permits capacity-driven overrides.

brian: Implementation plan: runtime will read `x-rw-sampled-override` or compute hash(req_id) fallback. Emit metric `trace.decisions{decision="hash"|"override_force"|"override_deny"}`. Also tag spans with `sampling.decider`.

maria: Need to confirm telemetry ingestion costs. If override forces more traces into ingest, ops wants a soft quota. Add metric `trace.ingest.estimate_bytes` per route so billing/alerts can fire.

taylor: For rollout UX: when user flips canary sampling to X% we should show expected sampled rate vs observed in last 5m and an escape button to revert. Also surface a link to example traces for that route (sampled only).

alice: Action items (owners + due dates):
- Edge: add `x-rw-request-id` generation when absent (maria) — due 1845200000
- Runtime: emit counters `request.total`, `request.with_request_id`, `trace.sampled.count`, `trace.decisions` + span tags (brian) — due 1845180000
- Platform/Grafana: add panels + alert when sampled_ratio > expected by 2x or traffic > ingest quota (taylor) — due 1845250000
- Console: add sampling override UI + per-route expected vs observed (taylor) — due 1845280000
- Docs: short spec for headers and deterministic sampling formula (sasha) — due 1845150000

brian: Quick example header set we plan to standardize: `x-rw-request-id: 123e4567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef`, `x-rw-sampled: 1`, `x-rw-sampled-override: force|deny|none`, `x-rw-request-source: edge|sdk|internal`.

sasha: Example deterministic code snippet: ```python
import hashlib
def is_sampled(req_id, pct):
    h = int(hashlib.sha1(req_id.encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16)
    return (h % 100) < pct
```

maria: Curl example to test headers: `curl -H "x-rw-request-id: test-123" -H "x-rw-sampled: 1" https://api.redwood.ai/route`

alice: Small ops question — are we okay with `trace.sampled.count` incrementing only when we actually send a trace to the ingest pipeline? Or should it increment for all logically-sampled requests even if we later drop due to quota?

brian: Plan: increment `trace.sampled.count` at decision time (logical sample). Emit `trace.ingest.sent` when we actually push to backend. That lets dashboards show decision vs ingest.

sasha: +1. That split is important for diagnosing drop behavior.

taylor: UX note: show both metrics on the route page and compute `ingest_loss = 1 - trace.ingest.sent / trace.sampled.count`. Good signal for capacity issues.

deploy-bot: deploy status: runtime sampling-metrics branch CI passed, canary queued.

alice: Thanks everyone. I'll synthesize a short spec doc from this thread and link it. If no objections, we'll treat these commits as dependent work and coordinate rollouts. :thumbsup:

maria: :+1:

sasha: will draft spec and ping for reviews.

brian: starting runtime PR tomorrow.

taylor: putting dashboard ticket in board now.

alice: closing loop — leaving this thread pinned until specs merged.
